name: Sweep from Zombie Guard
summary: A sweep from Zombie needs a controlled posting arm and an off-balanced base; the high rubber-guard connection alone does not guarantee a reversal or mount.
description: A sweep from Zombie needs a controlled posting arm and an off-balanced base; the high rubber-guard connection alone does not guarantee a reversal or mount.
overview:
The bottom player faces the opponent in Zombie, with a high leg controlling posture. The reviewed rubber-guard instruction supports controlling posture and a posting arm. It does not establish this node's unspecified direct sweep to mount; a specific sweep setup must be chosen before live practice.

Maintain posture control while freeing the other arm for the pummel. Determine which arm can prevent the intended reversal; do not assume an isolated arm removes every post. Use a safe wrist or arm connection without manipulating individual fingers.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Ben Eddy — the Zombie pummel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JzSxFvNA5Uo); [Brandon McCaghren — Gogoplata from rubber guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wn39-wrfsbs).

attacker.overview:
The bottom player faces the opponent in Zombie, with a high leg controlling posture. The reviewed rubber-guard instruction supports controlling posture and a posting arm. Maintain posture control while freeing the other arm for the pummel. Determine which arm can prevent the intended reversal; do not assume an isolated arm removes every post. Use a safe wrist or arm connection without manipulating individual fingers.

Use a small hip movement to check balance while retaining a stable guard. Proceed only after a coach has established the leg placement and direction for the chosen sweep. Release dangerous arm tension and establish the top position that actually results; mount requires additional leg clearance.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

The New York overhook can control one posting arm after the pummel, but it does not supply a complete sweep. If the base remains stable, guard retention needs a short hip escape and an inside frame against a crossface and chest pressure; a specific submission or reversal still needs its own demonstrated setup.

flashcards.question: Sweep from Zombie Guard (bottom): What does the Zombie action contribute to a sweep setup?
flashcards.answer: Zombie works on a posting arm from supported high guard; the resulting isolation is one possible ingredient in a separate sweep.
flashcards.answer_line: Clears a hand to isolate one arm

plausible: Removes the opposite knee post
Tips onto one hip before leg work

flashcards.question: Sweep from Zombie Guard (bottom): What must remain while the free hand pummels?
flashcards.answer: Keep the Mission Control connection while clearing the hand; without posture control the arm entry may not remain available.

plausible: Both hands at wrist, knee unbraced
Knee high, controlling hand lets go
trap: Ankle high, knee behind your hip

flashcards.question: Sweep from Zombie Guard (bottom): What should you assess after isolating one arm?
flashcards.answer: The other hand and the legs may still maintain base. Determine which support blocks the intended reversal before selecting a sweep.
flashcards.answer_line: The remaining hand and leg posts

plausible: Only grip on the wrist held outside
Only head height under the high shin
trap: Knee hug alone, ignoring far posts

flashcards.question: Sweep from Zombie Guard (bottom): Which control denies the free hand a post for the chosen tip?
flashcards.answer: Manage the arm as a whole so the hand cannot support weight in the chosen tipping direction. A grip alone is insufficient if the hand can still post; do not substitute individual finger leverage. This posting control supports a separately established sweep, not a complete Zombie sweep sequence.
flashcards.answer_line: Wrist or arm grip blocks hand post

plausible: Wrist touched, arm can reach the mat
Elbow held, hand still bears weight
trap: Let arm grip go as leaning starts

flashcards.question: Sweep from Zombie Guard (bottom): What can a small hip shift check before commitment?
flashcards.answer: A gentle balance check can reveal whether the base reacts while you still retain guard; it does not specify a full sweep.

plausible: Head lowers, both hands stay planted
Overhook tightens, their torso stays
trap: Your hips move, their weight stays

flashcards.question: Sweep from Zombie Guard (bottom): What can the overhook restrict after the hand clears?
flashcards.answer: The New York overhook can restrict the cleared arm. The other hand and the legs can still support weight, so a sweep needs its own setup.
flashcards.answer_line: One arm post; other supports remain

plausible: The opposite knee's supporting post
The far hand that still reaches mat
trap: Far hip without extra leg control

flashcards.question: Sweep from Zombie Guard (bottom): What determines the top position after a reversal?
flashcards.answer: Stabilize the actual landing; mount or side control requires its own body relationship beyond simply reversing top and bottom.
flashcards.answer_line: Landing and any legs still trapped

plausible: Hand clearance, ignoring leg ties
One retained overhook alone

flashcards.question: Sweep from Zombie Guard (bottom): Their base holds as posture escapes; what next?
flashcards.answer: If the pummel and proposed sweep do not retain posture, recover an inside knee and torso barrier before chasing another attack.

plausible: Keep arm grip with both knees passed
Lift foot before restoring knee room

flashcards.question: Sweep from Zombie Guard (bottom): Why release shoulder tension before changing direction?
flashcards.answer: Unload the captured shoulder before a large directional change so the proposed reversal does not become a forced joint lock.
flashcards.answer_line: Turning torso can twist a fixed arm

plausible: Loose overhook tips them your way
Low head lets caught elbow follow
trap: Fixed shoulder is a safe pivot

flashcards.question: Sweep from Zombie Guard (bottom): What should the first setup drill actually verify?
flashcards.answer: A cooperative drill can verify Zombie's arm-clearing checkpoint without claiming to have established the unspecified sweep.
flashcards.answer_line: Posture low; hand out; knee hugged

plausible: Head low, same hand still frames in
Hand on mat, high leg and hug loose

defender.description: Sweep from Zombie Guard (defender): Keep a useful forearm between the bodies before the bottom player gains the hand-clearing path. Move the whole arm rather than leaving the wrist exposed while the elbow remains fixed.
defender.overview:
The bottom player faces the opponent in Zombie, with a high leg controlling posture. The reviewed rubber-guard instruction supports controlling posture and a posting arm. It does not establish this node's unspecified direct sweep to mount; a specific sweep setup must be chosen before live practice.

Keep a useful forearm between the bodies before the bottom player gains the hand-clearing path. Move the whole arm rather than leaving the wrist exposed while the elbow remains fixed. The free hand working under yours is the cue to recover inside position before the knee hug closes.

Retract the elbow toward your ribs through available space, stopping if the shoulder is caught. Raise the chest after freeing the arm and reducing the high-leg control. Do not confuse an arm pummel with lockdown defense or apply twisting leg escapes to this upper-body exchange.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Use the early escape from the hand pummel to recover an inside elbow and a usable post. If that arm is already fixed for a submission, open the shoulder connection before attempting a large balance recovery.
key_principles: Maintain inside frames: Keep a useful forearm between the bodies before the bottom player gains the hand-clearing path.
Keep elbow and hand connected: Move the whole arm rather than leaving the wrist exposed while the elbow remains fixed.
Notice the pummel early: The free hand working under yours is the cue to recover inside position before the knee hug closes.
Recover without yanking: Retract the elbow toward your ribs through available space, stopping if the shoulder is caught.
Rebuild posture gradually: Raise the chest after freeing the arm and reducing the high-leg control.
Respect the high guard: Do not confuse an arm pummel with lockdown defense or apply twisting leg escapes to this upper-body exchange.

flashcards.question: Sweep from Zombie Guard (top): What limits the initial posting-arm capture?
flashcards.answer: Early inside position can deny the Zombie pummel and preserve usable arm support before the knee hug closes.

plausible: Wide mat hand outside their hip
Both arms over their shoulders

flashcards.question: Sweep from Zombie Guard (top): What should accompany a wrist recovery?
flashcards.answer: Move hand and elbow together so the wrist is not left outside a fixed arm line during balance recovery.
flashcards.answer_line: The elbow returning toward your ribs

plausible: Only hand in; elbow stays flared
Free hand posts wide, caught arm out
trap: Chest turns away, caught elbow fixed

flashcards.question: Sweep from Zombie Guard (top): Which cue warns your posting arm may be removed?
flashcards.answer: Recognize the under-hand pummel before the opponent covers the arm and secures the knee hug.

plausible: Their free foot returns to the floor
Hips move while hands stay free
trap: Hand circles head after knee hug set

flashcards.question: Sweep from Zombie Guard (top): What must precede a large turn with the arm already fixed?
flashcards.answer: If the knee hug fixes the arm, open that connection before a large balance-recovery turn rather than rotating through the joint.

plausible: Only widen knees, wrist stays pinned
Only post free hand farther away
trap: Free wrist only, elbow stays pinned
